explanation: Group equal values, sort the groups by descending frequency, and return the first k keys. The contract guarantees a unique top-k set.
timeComplexity: O(n + u log u) time for n values and u distinct values. Counting consumes n values; ordering u frequency records costs O(u log(u+1)); taking k keys costs O(k).
spaceComplexity: O(n + u) auxiliary space for grouping and sorting, plus O(k) output. Grouping retains occurrences and sorting retains group references; the returned array stores k keys.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Grouping counts every occurrence of each distinct value. Sorting groups by descending count places all more frequent values first. Selecting the first k groups therefore returns exactly the top-k set; the promised strict boundary removes ambiguity about membership.
walkthrough: For [4,4,4,7,7,9] and k=2, frequencies are 4→3,7→2,9→1. Descending frequency order is 4,7,9, so the top two values are [4,7], in either accepted order.
edgeCases: k may equal the number of distinct values.
The kth frequency must exceed the next frequency when another value exists.
